summary.text: George McDermott, a Republican and victim rights advocate, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Maryland's 4th Congressional District to Glenn Ivey.
He ran for this seat several times, in the Democratic primary in 2012 and as the Republican nominee in 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2024.

paragraphs.text: According to Ballotpedia, McDermott earned a trade school diploma and has worked as a victim rights advocate.
He ran in the 2012 Democratic primary for the 4th District, losing to incumbent Donna Edwards (5.1% to her 91.8%), and in the 2014 Republican primary, losing to Nancy Hoyt.
McDermott won the 2016 Republican primary and lost the general election to Anthony Brown, and he ran again as the Republican nominee in 2018 (19.9%) and 2020 (20.2%), losing to Brown both times.
He was the Republican nominee in 2024, losing to Glenn Ivey, 88.4% to 11.2%.
In 2026 he advanced from the June 23 Republican primary as the only candidate on the ballot, receiving 1,923 votes.
He received 6.2% of the vote to Glenn Ivey's 89.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
